findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:1216-1221 (writeCodexProcessEvent) excludes ONLY entry.command==="quorum_submit" from the generic post-handler codex_cli process-event append, with a comment stating this is because quorum_submit "owns one exact immutable process-events transaction inside its handler" and a generic append "would make that canonical commit dirty again". quorum_prune (packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-prune.ts:20-22,338-365) commits process-events.jsonl through the IDENTICAL captureLifecycleMetadataTransaction/commitLifecycleMetadataTransaction machinery and its own header comment explicitly claims parity ("committed through the SAME lifecycle-metadata transaction machinery quorum_submit uses so the pre-dirty refusal, exact-content verification, and rollback all hold") — a claim also repeated in command-policy.ts:480 and process-fact-levels.ts:209, both touched by this diff. cli-engine.ts was NOT updated to add the matching exclusion for quorum_prune. Live repro (built dist, temp git fixture, LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex): `lattice quorum_prune --apply` succeeds and commits cleanly (HEAD advances, applied:true), but immediately after, `git status --porcelain` shows `M .lattice/story/actives/<id>/process-events.jsonl` — the exact file quorum_prune just atomically committed is re-dirtied by the unguarded generic codex_cli append, which is the precise poisoning mode the sibling comment for quorum_submit exists to prevent. This leftover dirty state then makes quorum_prune/quorum_submit pre-dirty-refuse on the very next call for reasons unrelated to genuine story changes. No test in packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts exercises `quorum_prune --apply` through the real CLI (runFixtureCli, which sets LATTICE_ACTIVITY_SOURCE=codex) with a post-command git-status-clean assertion (unlike the existing quorum_submit CLI test at line ~939 which does assert `git status --porcelain=v1===`), so this gap is untested. WHY: the diff repeatedly promises quorum_prune has transactional parity with quorum_submit including pre-dirty-refusal integrity, but the one cross-file wiring point that actually protects that guarantee under Codex-driven sessions was left half-registered.

handlers/quorum-prune.ts:125-135 writeUniqueBackup() writes the pre-prune backup directly into the git-tracked story dir (.lattice/story/actives/<id>/process-events.jsonl.bak-<ts>) and NEVER stages/commits/gitignores it (no matching *.bak-* gitignore pattern; the *.bak pattern at .gitignore does not match the .bak-<timestamp> suffix). Verified live: after `quorum_prune {apply:true}` succeeds, `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` in the story dir shows `?? .../process-events.jsonl.bak-<ts>` (repro output captured). Both assertCleanPruneBaseline (quorum-prune.ts:112-123, called at :336) and assertCleanQuorumBaseline (quorum-submit.ts:219-228, called at :529) do a raw whole-tree `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` with zero exemption for this file, so the very first legitimate follow-up action after a successful recovery -- another quorum_prune apply, OR a genuinely-new quorum_submit once the story-owned files change -- throws "worktree/index must be clean"/"nothing to prune" refusals caused entirely by the tool's own leftover backup, not by real user dirt. The same unexempted --untracked-files=all pattern is reused broadly (validation-executor.ts:202, done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts:362, dirty-worktree-gate.ts:42, recover-evidence.ts:68, cross-host-review.ts:81), so a leftover backup can also block TEST/DONE-adjacent gates. This directly undermines the story's stated goal ("the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level" / official low-friction recovery) since the operator must now manually discover and clean up (commit, delete, or gitignore) the tool's own artifact before doing anything else in the story. None of the 12 quorum_prune smoke checks catch this: the one test that runs quorum_prune apply twice ("never overwrites a previous run backup") masks it by doing its own `git add -A; git commit` between the two applies, which incidentally absorbs the first backup file into a commit -- a step a real operator/recovery workflow would not necessarily perform.

CHK-002:edge:2 evidence overclaims, packages/main/src/handlers/quorum-submit.ts:519-526 vs packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1665-1669: intent requires the refusal message to be verified as naming standing runIds, materialDigest of the standing verdicts, and pointing at review_escalation_status. The production message does contain all of that, but the ONLY assertion against it anywhere in the smoke suite is assert.match(..., /quorum_submit refuses: .*drift-accept/i, ...) at line 1667 (and /drift-accept/i at 1711/1714) -- neither checks for runIds, materialDigest values, or the literal string review_escalation_status. The verificationEvidence note for CHK-002:edge:2 ("Drift-branch message content asserted via regex; message names standing runIds, older material(s), current storyFilesHash, poisoning consequence, and points at review_escalation_status") overstates what the bound regex actually verifies -- it is true of the production code, not of the test assertion.

CHK-003:happy:2 evidence cites an unbound command, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2098-2113: the checklist scope.allowedModify explicitly includes packages/main/src/core/config.ts (DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS wiring), and config.ts:362 does add quorum_prune to DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS. But the bound checks own comment (~2106-2109) says exercising that wiring is "outside this storys scope contract" and is not tested there (only catalog+policy resolution and non-unknown-command dispatch are asserted). The verificationEvidence note for CHK-003:happy:2 instead claims coverage via "scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs passes with the new fact row and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS entry" -- but that script is a different, separate command from the one this evidence row is bound to (node packages/main/dist/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.js), and no verificationEvidence row records that script having been run at this headHash/materialHash. The claimed "wiring verification across all 5 integration points" is therefore not actually demonstrated by evidence bound to this storys own smoke command for the config.ts integration point.

CHK-002:adversarial:2 evidence overclaims, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1622-1673: intent explicitly requires asserting hostVerdictEventCount, verdictFileCount, AND `git rev-parse HEAD` all unchanged after the drift-accept refusal (does not advance HEAD). The bound check (refuses a redundant re-submit when the standing quorum drift-accepts) captures beforeEvents/beforeVerdicts (lines 1640-1641) and asserts them unchanged (lines 1670-1671), but never captures or re-checks `git rev-parse HEAD` before/after the refusal -- unlike every other refusal-leaks-no-state check in this same file (e.g. lines 1545/1552, 1740/1745, 1877/1890, 1943/1951) which do assert HEAD is unchanged via beforeHead. One of the three required invariants in this adversarial intent is unverified.

CHK-001:edge:0 evidence reuses happy:1 assertion, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:1622-1673 (lines 1633-1636): the intent explicitly states storyFilesHash equality is necessary but not sufficient and requires an independent check that commitMainDrift touches zero story-owned file blobs. The bound evidence reuses the exact same storyHashBefore===storyHashAfter assertion already used for CHK-001:happy:1 -- no distinct file-level/diff-based assertion exists anywhere in the suite verifying commitMainDrift only ever touches main-drift.ts; this is proven only by the note ("commitMainDrift helper commits only ... - no story-diff file is touched"), which is a claim about the helpers hardcoded implementation, not an independent runtime check as the intent explicitly demanded.

CHK-003 (quorum_prune) test-coverage gap, packages/main/src/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2245-2268: no check anywhere in the 12 quorum_prune checks asserts the worktree is clean immediately after a successful `quorum_prune {apply:true}`. quorum-prune.ts:161-169 lifecycleMetadataPaths(kind=quorum-submit) scopes the commit to ONLY process-events.jsonl; writeUniqueBackup() (quorum-prune.ts:125-135, called at :351) writes process-events.jsonl.bak-<timestamp> directly into the tracked story dir and it is never staged/committed by that scoped transaction. .gitignore:32 `*.bak` does not match the `.bak-<timestamp>` suffix, so the backup is left untracked. assertCleanPruneBaseline/assertCleanQuorumBaseline both run an unscoped `git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all`, so the very next quorum_prune or quorum_submit call would refuse on the tools own leftover artifact -- verified live by re-running quorum_prune {apply:true} in a fresh fixture right after a first apply with no intervening commit: it refuses nothing-to-prune only after the backup is manually cleaned. The ONE check that runs prune twice (quorum-submit-smoke.ts:2245 never overwrites a previous run backup) masks this because it does its own git add -A + commit between the two applies (lines ~2261-2262), which is not a step a real recovery operator performs. So CHK-003 happy path claim (userSees: the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level / official low-friction recovery) is unverified at the worktree-cleanliness level and is contradicted once you try the very next legitimate action. (Independently corroborates a live concurrent lattice-review-quality RR-003 finding on the same defect, verified here from the test-coverage angle: no verificationEvidence row demonstrates clean-after-apply.)
